description: Normative Test8 contract reference. Contracts define harness behavior without making implementation or tests authoritative.

authority.implementationRole: Implementation files realize these contracts but cannot redefine them.
authority.testRole: Tests are verification evidence and regression protection only; a test cannot create, weaken, or replace a contract.
authority.nonRedefinitionRule: This file defines Test8 harness behavior and does not redefine repository conventions, convention profile meaning, exemption approval, publication, release, deployment, or operations policy.

terminology.profile: A named directory under the bundled src/checks tree.
terminology.check: One bundled module responsible for one exact directive identity.
terminology.ruleId: An exact E- or A-prefixed directive identifier, including all numeric components.
terminology.parentRuleId: The nearest directive represented by the containing check directory.
terminology.selectedCheck: A discovered check belonging to an explicitly selected profile.
terminology.exemptedCheck: A selected check excluded by its own exemption or an exemption on an ancestor rule.
terminology.diagnostic: A stable human-readable description of a validation failure or internal validation error.

contractConventions.directiveIds: References are to local Test8 directives only; repository convention IDs remain authoritative in eliware/conventions.
contractConventions.contract: The exact inputs, outputs, errors, ordering, and invariants for one cohesive harness behavior.
contractConventions.verification: Non-authoritative tests and commands used to verify the contract.
contractConventions.parent: Optional contract hierarchy reference; referenced parents must exist and cycles are prohibited.
contractConventions.dependencies: Optional cross-contract ordering or dependency references.

contracts.title: CLI entry and informational dispatch
dos: Keep bin/eliware-test.mjs limited to process wiring and pass process.argv.slice(2) to the CLI.
Treat --help and --version as informational commands that perform no validation and return 0.
Use a writer callback for output, defaulting to console.log.
donts: Do not expose internal modules as the consumer CLI boundary.
Do not perform repository validation for informational commands.

inputs.args: An ordered array of CLI argument strings.
inputs.write: Optional function receiving one output string at a time.
inputs.root: Optional validation root; defaults to process.cwd().

outputs.version: The package version string when --version is present.
outputs.help: The supported usage string when --help is present.

errors: Informational command failures are reported through the normal harness failure boundary.
ordering: Recognize --version/--help before validation or stage execution.
invariants: Informational commands return 0 when their output is written successfully.

contracts.title: CLI validation dispatch and diagnostics
dos: Run the bundled convention-validation path for a normal invocation.
Return code 18 for convention, configuration, argument, or harness failures.
Preserve every failed-check diagnostic and optionally append one timing diagnostic when requested.
donts: Do not run unrelated publication, deployment, release, synchronization, or external package commands as validation side effects.
Do not erase an earlier diagnostic when a later operation fails.

errors: Thrown orchestration errors become code 18 with their message as a diagnostic.
ordering: Read options, run validation, write stage diagnostics, then write optional timing.
invariants: Successful validation returns code 0 and an empty diagnostics list.

contracts.title: Repository configuration loading
dos: Read package.json before selecting or executing checks.
Require valid harness configuration before partial validation begins.
Keep applicability selection explicit rather than inferring it from repository shape.
donts: Do not start check execution with missing, malformed, empty, or unknown harness configuration.

outputs.configuration: { apply: string[] } with validated harness applicability.

errors: Missing or malformed configuration throws a descriptive configuration error.
ordering: Configuration validation precedes check discovery for selection and check execution.

contracts.title: Bundled check discovery and registry integrity
dos: Discover checks recursively from the published src/checks filesystem.
Use profile directories and directive-named modules as the runtime registry.
Validate module identity, entry points, parentage, duplicates, and deterministic numeric ordering.
donts: Do not fetch a private conventions repository or silently overwrite duplicate or malformed checks.

inputs.options: Optional injectable root, directory reader, and module importer.

outputs.checks: Ordered records containing ruleId, optional parentRuleId, and run.

errors: Unknown profile, duplicate rule ID, invalid module export, or invalid rule filename fails discovery.
ordering: Sort by numeric rule components, using lexical comparison only as a final tie-breaker.
invariants: A module filename and exported ruleId always identify the same rule.
Parentage is derived from containing rule-named directories.

contracts.title: Check result and validation context
dos: Require every check to return one result with its exact rule ID and a pass or fail status.
Supply checks with the target root and parsed package metadata.
donts: Do not expose warning, skipped, unknown, partial, or not-applicable result states.

inputs.context: { root, packageJson } unless a documented extension adds more fields.

errors: A missing, malformed, or mismatched result throws an invalid-check-result error.
ordering: Result validation occurs immediately after each check returns.
invariants: Check modules do not mutate shared orchestration state to communicate results.

contracts.title: Profile selection and exemption execution
dos: Execute only checks selected by validated profiles.
Validate exemption IDs against the complete bundled registry.
Skip an exempted rule and every descendant in its parentRuleId chain while preserving unrelated siblings.
donts: Do not let check modules infer applicability or exemption state, and do not let an unknown exemption silently skip work.

outputs.results: Non-exempt CheckResults in deterministic execution order.

errors: Unknown exemption IDs and thrown check errors fail validation.
ordering: Check ancestors are evaluated for exemption before the check runs.
Checks run sequentially in discovery order.
invariants: An exact exemption excludes no sibling branch.
An ancestor exemption excludes all discovered descendants.

contracts.title: Validation stage aggregation and exit semantics
dos: Aggregate all failed-check diagnostics deterministically.
Use stable exit categories and preserve every diagnostic.
donts: Do not convert an unknown, skipped, partial, or failed required operation into success.

errors: A thrown callback error produces code 18 and one safe diagnostic.
ordering: Failure diagnostics follow check result order.
invariants: All-pass results produce code 0 and no diagnostics.

contracts.title: Focused execution
dos: Expose focused testing through the public harness boundary.
Reject missing or ambiguous focused paths before unrelated execution.
Scope coverage to an unambiguous mirrored source mapping.
donts: Do not silently fall back to the full suite or report unrelated-module coverage failures for a focused request.

inputs.focusedPaths: Recognized test paths supplied through the public invocation.

outputs.scope: Only requested tests and unambiguously mapped source coverage are selected.

errors: Unsupported, missing, or ambiguous paths produce the stable convention failure result.
invariants: Focused selection does not add profiles or change exemption evaluation.

contracts.title: Coverage summary and 100×4 evaluation
dos: Evaluate statements, branches, functions, and lines independently against exactly 100.
Accept usable JSON totals or a usable Jest text summary fallback.
Reject stale, changing, invalid, missing, or zero-valued evidence as appropriate.
donts: Do not treat missing instrumented entries or incomplete metrics as successful coverage.

inputs.summary: Coverage metric object or report reader inputs.
inputs.report: Optional report path and freshness clock/stat seams.

errors: Invalid or stale reports throw descriptive coverage errors.
ordering: Freshness is checked before and during report reading.
invariants: Any metric other than exactly 100 appears in gaps.
The four metrics are never collapsed into one aggregate percentage.

contracts.title: Process and external-state boundaries
dos: Use Node child-process APIs and argument arrays.
Bound captured output and preserve actionable failure context.
Keep validation read-only with respect to external systems.
donts: Do not depend on shell pipelines, shell quoting, platform-specific executable assumptions, or unbounded output capture.
Do not publish, deploy, release, synchronize, tag, or push during validation.

inputs.command: Executable and argument array supplied to a process adapter.

outputs.process: Bounded stdout/stderr and normalized process status.

errors: Spawn, timeout, nonzero status, and output-limit failures preserve safe context.
ordering: Argument construction is separate from process execution.
invariants: External state is not mutated by validation.
Sensitive values are excluded from diagnostics.

contracts.title: Orchestration composition boundaries
dos: Keep orchestrators responsible for composition, ordering, and dependency injection.
Keep check and process modules responsible for their own focused business logic.
Allow filesystem, process, clock, and package seams to be injected for deterministic verification.
donts: Do not make a coordinator absorb unrelated check logic or require consumers to import internal orchestration modules.

inputs.dependencies: Explicit functions or adapters supplied at composition boundaries.

outputs.pipeline: Stable stage or check results without hidden side effects.

errors: Dependency failures retain their original safe context.
ordering: Composition determines stage order; subordinate modules do not secretly reorder peer work.
invariants: A new responsibility is represented by a focused module rather than appended to an unrelated module.

contracts.title: Contract traceability and verification boundary
dos: Keep each contract individually identifiable and traceable to implementation and verification evidence.
Use tests as evidence that contracts are fulfilled, not as the source of contract truth.
Keep contract references repository-relative and reviewable.
donts: Do not let implementation behavior or a passing test silently redefine a contract.

inputs.contract: One atomic record from this file.

outputs.traceability: A reviewer can identify the responsible implementation and verification evidence for each contract.

errors: Missing or invalid contract references are documentation/contract review failures.
ordering: Contract definition precedes implementation and verification evidence.
invariants: The contract document remains authoritative for harness behavior even when implementation or tests are incomplete.
